Merge PDF files in your browser

Open your first PDF below, then add more files from the Pages panel. You can drag pages into a new order, delete the ones you don't need, and save the result as one PDF. Your device combines the files, and no server is involved.

You can also export only the pages you select as a separate file.

Prefer it in Chrome? Install the Quire PDF extension

This tool opens your PDF on this device and never uploads it.

How it works

  1. Open the first PDF with the Open button, or drop it on the tool.

  2. Click Pages in the toolbar to show the page thumbnails.

  3. Click the + (Add file) button at the top of the panel and choose one or more PDFs. Their pages are added after the current page.

  4. Drag thumbnails to reorder. To remove pages, select them, open Manage and choose Delete.

  5. Click Save a copy to download the combined PDF.

Questions

Questions and limits

What this tool does and what it can't do.

Is there a limit on how many files I can merge?

There is no limit on the number of files, but the combined PDF must stay under 100 MB, and very large documents depend on how much memory your device has.

Why was a file rejected when I tried to combine it?

If two PDFs contain form fields with the same name, Quire refuses to combine them, because the merged form would mix up their values. Flatten one of them in another tool first, or combine forms that use different field names.

Can I copy or duplicate pages?

Not in this version. Copy, cut and paste of pages are switched off. You can reorder, delete, add pages from another file and export selected pages.

Is my PDF uploaded anywhere?

No. The page and its PDF engine (Mozilla's PDF.js) load from quireapps.com. After that, your browser opens, edits and saves the file inside this tab and never sends it to a server. The page has no analytics or tracking. To check, open your browser's developer tools and watch the Network tab.

Is it free? Do I need an account?

It is free, and you don't need an account. The tool adds no watermark and has no daily limit. Files can be up to 100 MB.

Which browsers does it work in?

Testing covers Chromium-based browsers such as Chrome and Edge. PDF.js, the engine underneath, also runs in current Firefox and Safari, but those have had less testing here. In Chrome and Edge, Save a copy lets you pick where the file goes. Other browsers download it.
